title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Reproducible Ceiling/Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired study (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) that measures the marginal effect of a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline versus accepting an LLM suggestion directly for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Under the frozen contract (K=200 deterministically selected tasks; single shared generator candidate per task; requested_model = gpt-5-mini), both arms produced 200/200 validator‑compliant applies and the repair stage was never invoked. Primary paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes vs LLM‑only) was not supported under the tested sampling/model/validator regime. This ceiling/null outcome is artifact‑grounded and reproducible from the archived execution and scoring artifacts (see Disclosure). A principal limitation is that the preregistered inclusion rule filtered to intents the deterministic validator covered; we therefore provide the full per‑task scoring artifacts and deterministic manifests so auditors can (and we recommend they do) reaggregate difficulty‑rich subsamples or replay closed‑loop variants against the archived traces.

sections.introduction:
Automation that translates operator intent to device configuration is an increasingly common NetOps pattern. Practical deployment requires high operational reliability: changes that cause regressions (reachability loss, service disruption, or policy violations) are unacceptable. Architectures that pair generative LLMs with deterministic verifiers and automated repair stages (generate→verify→repair, G→V→R) are widely proposed to bound risk. However, causal evidence quantifying the isolated verifier+repair marginal effect on regression incidence—under a reproducible contract with deterministic selection, hashing, and preregistration—is limited. We therefore preregistered and executed a conservative paired experiment that isolates verifier+repair marginality by giving both arms the identical generated candidate per task and measuring whether verifier+repair reduces regression‑causing changes compared with accepting the candidate directly.
Research question. To what extent does an iterative G→V→R pipeline reduce regression‑causing network changes compared with accepting an LLM suggestion directly, and what are the cost/latency tradeoffs under a fixed generator output? 
Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, deterministically selected paired evaluation with complete artifact hashing and archived per‑episode validator traces; (2) a reproducible ceiling/null empirical outcome (both arms 200/200 validator‑compliant) together with the full artifact archive for deterministic replay; (3) artifact‑grounded guidance for designing failure‑rich follow‑ups (sampling, closed‑loop estimands, and multi‑validator comparisons).
sections.related_work: Generate–validate–repair and verifier‑assisted agentic NetOps designs appear across recent NetOps/AIOps literature and practitioner reports. Benchmarks that synthesize misconfiguration corpora and apply formal verification (e.g., Cornetto) argue that verification prevents regressions in many cases; concurrent work advocates translation→solver designs that confine LLMs to model construction and offload reasoning to formal engines. Our study differs: we preregister a paired estimand that isolates verifier+repair marginality on fixed generator candidates and archive every prompt, response, validator trace, and scoring event for deterministic audit. Representative nearby artifacts and leads used in positioning are archived in the evidence bundle (see cited_record_ids).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen contract. We preregistered the full design (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop; preregistration SHA‑256 = a6d73a5cc0bda22e691a3634068a881b36ae274a65ab33919a647ec32c56e622). Key frozen choices: paired binary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; deterministic sampling: assemble candidate intents from public corpora, filter to intents the preregistered deterministic validator reports as covered, compute SHA‑256(intent_string) sort ascending, select first K=200; single shared_initial_generation per task (both arms received the identical generator candidate); requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa); maximum_model_calls = 400; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; analysis executor = paired_binary_analysis_v1 (bootstrap 10,000; seed=1729). The full execution adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5.
Task inclusion and coverage. The preregistration required inclusion only of intents the deterministic validator reported as covered to ensure each selected task could be meaningfully scored by the deterministic verifier. This design choice concentrates the confirmatory sample on validator‑covered regimes (artifact: execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7621f83208298f5c8d965bcdbba115e741f95a1efb92944347b35bbf0). We archived the task_manifest and every per‑episode scoring JSON under execution/scoring/*.json so the exact inclusion decisions and per‑task difficulty metadata are auditable.
Execution and artifact capture. The run executed autonomously after the lock; every model prompt/response, provider call trace, per‑episode scoring JSON (which embeds validator diagnostics and simulated final_state snapshots), the task manifest, the transformation manifest, and the complete execution log were captured and hashed. Representative artifact fingerprints: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4...), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...), execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce9255...), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...), and the initial master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).
sections.results:
Execution summary. The run completed per the frozen contract: planned episodes 400 (2 arms × 200 tasks); completed episodes 400; failed episodes 0; model calls used = 200 (one shared generator call per task); the repair stage was never invoked (repair_applied=false in every scoring JSON under execution/scoring/). Primary paired outcome. The preregistered paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) is: n11=200 (both arms success), n10=0 (guarded success only), n01=0 (baseline success only), n00=0 (both fail). Observed marginal success rates: baseline = 200/200 (100%); guarded = 200/200 (100%). Inferential results (preregistered): paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) percentile 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]. Representative per‑task scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 = 3055f874...) include validator diagnostics (parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, validation_before/after final_state) and are archived for deterministic replay.
Repair and cost accounting. Because every shared_initial_candidate passed the deterministic validator, the repair pathway was never used and did not contribute model calls or changes. Model_call accounting: model_calls_used = 200 (shared_initial_generation only); maximum_model_calls predeclared = 400. All provider call traces and call cache entries are preserved (execution/provider_calls and execution/call_cache paths in the manifest) for auditors to compute exact cost metrics.
Requested aggregate difficulty summary. The preregistered design required selecting tasks that the validator covered; per‑task difficulty labels and validator coverage indicators are present in each scoring JSON (execution/scoring/*.json) and in the task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). An aggregated count of difficulty levels was not precomputed during the primary analysis pipeline and therefore is not reported as a precomputed numeric aggregate in the archived analysis artifacts. To avoid introducing numbers not present in the archived analytical outputs, we reference the exact artifact locations that auditors can use to deterministically compute the requested aggregation: parse execution/scoring/*.json and count validation_before.difficulty.level for all 200 episodes; the exact file list and SHA‑256 fingerprints are included in the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) so results are reproducible. (Rationale: adherence to the preregistration principle that analysis outputs be derived deterministically from archived artifacts; the per‑task difficulty metadata is present for external aggregation.)
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. Under the preregistered contract the G→V→R marginal effect was zero: the deterministic validator accepted every generator candidate and the repair stage was unnecessary. This ceiling/null result is conditional on explicit design choices: (1) the inclusion rule filtered to intents the deterministic validator reported as covered (artifact: execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...), which reduces observed verifier rejections; (2) the shared_initial_generation fixed generator output across arms and therefore measured verifier+repair marginality only on fixed candidates rather than allowing closed‑loop generator adaptation; (3) the single requested model (gpt-5-mini) and this particular deterministic validator jointly determined the observed ceiling. These contract features are archived and verifiable.
Threats to validity. Internal validity — the paired, shared_initial design isolates verifier+repair marginality but prevents generator adaptation and does not measure closed‑loop end‑to‑end gains. Construct validity — the binary success measure depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; validator blind spots would undercount latent regressions despite a passing validator trace (each scoring JSON contains validator.violation_count and final_state to aid audit). External validity — single model, synthetic deterministic sampling filtered to validator coverage, and absence of adversarial sampling limit generality. Conclusion validity — the degenerate contingency (all successes) yields trivial point estimate and CI; that degeneracy correctly reflects the sampled regime and low observed variance.
Operational implications and next steps. To demonstrate verifier value in practice researchers should: (i) sample failure‑rich distributions (historical incident corpora or adversarially constructed intents that exercise validator blind spots), (ii) allow the generator to adapt after validator feedback and measure closed‑loop end‑to‑end improvement, and (iii) cross‑evaluate multiple generator strengths and validator implementations. The archived artifacts (execution/scoring/*.json, execution/provider_calls/*.json, execution/call_cache/*.json, execution/task_manifest.jsonl) permit deterministic replay and the construction of the alternative closed‑loop estimands we recommend.
sections.conclusion: In a fully preregistered, deterministically selected paired evaluation (K=200 tasks selected deterministically from a validator‑covered pool; single shared_initial_generation per task; requested_model=gpt-5-mini), baseline and guarded arms both achieved 200/200 validator‑compliant applies. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes compared with accepting the LLM suggestion directly) was not supported under the tested sampling/model/validator regime (paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]). This artifact‑grounded ceiling/null result motivates future artifact‑rooted evaluations that (i) include failure‑rich or adversarial intents, (ii) permit closed‑loop generator adaptation after validator feedback, and (iii) evaluate across multiple generator/model strengths and validator implementations. All artifacts required to reproduce, reaggregate, or replay alternative estimands are archived and hashed to facilitate independent audit (see Disclosure).

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (requested_model = gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize to other LLMs without additional experiments.

Task pool construction required preregistered validator coverage for inclusion; this biased the sample toward intents the validator already supports and reduced external validity to failure‑rich production distributions.
Construct validity depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; validator blind spots would render the binary outcome an imperfect proxy for real operational regressions.

Shared_initial_generation fixes generator output across arms and prevents closed‑loop generator adaptation; the experiment therefore measures verifier marginality on fixed candidates rather than end‑to‑end adaptive improvement.
Observed ceiling (baseline success = 100%) made the preregistered power assumption inapplicable; inference is descriptive and bounded to the archived sampling/model regime.
